Intel (INTC) ended the recent trading session at $101.40, demonstrating a -3.15% change from the preceding day's closing price. This move lagged the S&P 500's daily loss of 0.06%. Meanwhile, the Dow experienced a rise of 0.38%, and the technology-dominated Nasdaq saw a decrease of 0.44%.

Heading into today, shares of the world's largest chipmaker had gained 1.71% over the past month, lagging the Computer and Technology sector's gain of 4.85% and the S&P 500's gain of 2.36%.

The investment community will be closely monitoring the performance of Intel in its forthcoming earnings report. The company is scheduled to release its earnings on October 29, 2026. The company is expected to report EPS of $0.38, up 65.22% from the prior-year quarter. Meanwhile, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for revenue is projecting net sales of $16.36 billion, up 19.82% from the year-ago period.

For the full year, the Zacks Consensus Estimates are projecting earnings of $1.5 per share and revenue of $62.27 billion, which would represent changes of +257.14% and +17.82%, respectively, from the prior year.

Investors should also note any recent changes to analyst estimates for Intel. These revisions typically reflect the latest short-term business trends, which can change frequently. Hence, positive alterations in estimates signify analyst optimism regarding the business and profitability.

Our research demonstrates that these adjustments in estimates directly associate with imminent stock price performance. Investors can capitalize on this by using the Zacks Rank. This model considers these estimate changes and provides a simple, actionable rating system.

Ranging from #1 (Strong Buy) to #5 (Strong Sell), the Zacks Rank system has a proven, outside-audited track record of outperformance, with #1 stocks returning an average of +25% annually since 1988. Within the past 30 days, our consensus EPS projection remained stagnant. As of now, Intel holds a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold).

Looking at its valuation, Intel is holding a Forward P/E ratio of 69.83. This signifies a premium in comparison to the average Forward P/E of 33.56 for its industry.

It's also important to note that INTC currently trades at a PEG ratio of 7.76. The PEG ratio is similar to the widely-used P/E ratio, but this metric also takes the company's expected earnings growth rate into account. The Semiconductor - General was holding an average PEG ratio of 1.77 at yesterday's closing price.

The Semiconductor - General industry is part of the Computer and Technology sector. This industry currently has a Zacks Industry Rank of 46, which puts it in the top 19% of all 250+ industries.

title: What Changed In Qualcomm's Story?
detail:
What Changed In Qualcomm's Story?
Trefis Team
Mon, October 12, 2026 at 2:55 PM PDT 4 min read
QCOM
^GSPC
AVGO
NVDA
INTC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Qualcomm (QCOM) stock is currently priced at 20.0 times earnings, trading below the 21.9 multiple of the S&P 500. Investors paying that price need a clear understanding of what they are buying, particularly as the company shifts its public priorities. Back in July 2025, executives anchored their presentations on sales targets for automotive and IoT chips, which power connected consumer and industrial devices. By the latest call, those figures had taken a back seat. So what does Qualcomm lead with now?

Qualcomm Is Entering A New Chip Market

Executives are now highlighting chips for data centers, a market the company is only just entering. During the fiscal Q3 2026 earnings call in July 2026, management stated that Qualcomm was "expanding into the data center with 4 unique product lines."

That represents a distinct shift in messaging. During the fiscal Q3 2025 call a year earlier, leadership instead focused on a fiscal 2029 target of $22 billion in combined automotive and IoT revenue.

Those alternative revenue streams remain critical because Qualcomm relies heavily on smartphones. Its chip business made up 87% of revenue in fiscal 2025, and phones generated $5.1 billion of that segment's $8.5 billion in revenue during fiscal Q3 2026. And on its July 2026 call, Qualcomm said it expected its share of the then-upcoming iPhone launch to be materially lower than its prior estimate of 20%. Management characterizes this push beyond phones as its diversification strategy.

How Big Are Qualcomm's Old And New Priorities?

Qualcomm already reports its automotive and IoT results, whereas the data center business remains mostly a forecast. The company posted automotive revenue of $1.6 billion in fiscal Q3 2026, marking a 61% increase from a year earlier. In the same period, IoT revenue grew 9% to $1.8 billion.

The data center operation is still in its earliest stages. Wafer production has begun on Qualcomm's two custom data center chip wins, and these components are due to start generating revenue in the December quarter. Looking further out, management forecast data center revenue of $5 billion in fiscal 2027.

Automotive and IoT products still represent the larger piece of management's long-term plan. Executives now expect to generate more than $24 billion from cars and IoT in fiscal 2029, compared to more than $15 billion from data centers. The total fiscal 2029 outlook for sales outside phones currently stands at $40 billion.

Can Qualcomm Investors Take Comfort In This?

For the automotive and IoT segments, the internal projections offer reassurance. Management maintained and even expanded its prior targets: the car and IoT portion of the fiscal 2029 outlook is now larger than the forecast provided in July 2025. The company also guided for another record automotive performance in fiscal Q4 2026, projecting revenue growth of approximately 60% from a year earlier.

title: Is ASML Holding NV's Stock a Buy Ahead of Its Q3 Earnings Report Wednesday?
detail:
Is ASML Holding NV's Stock a Buy Ahead of Its Q3 Earnings Report Wednesday?
Jeremy Bowman, The Motley Fool

ASML
NVDA
TSM
INTC
005930.KS
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

ASML (NASDAQ:ASML) doesn't get as much attention as chip stocks like Nvidia do, but the European semiconductor capital equipment specialist is arguably just as crucial to the AI boom.

ASML is the world's only manufacturer of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography equipment, which is used by manufacturers like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, Intel, and Samsung to make the world's most advanced chips.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The company is downstream from fabless chip companies like Nvidia in the AI boom, but it's set to reap the rewards of surging demand for AI chips, including the memory chip shortage and the supply expansion now underway.

With ASML set to report third-quarter earnings on Wednesday, let's review what to expect from the company to determine if the stock is a buy.

Image source: Image source: The Motley Fool.

Can ASML keep climbing?

ASML stock is up 64% this year, benefiting from the larger boom in chip stocks in the spring, though it's traded sideways over the last few months.

Investors bid the stock up on expectations that its growth will accelerate due to semiconductor supply shortages, and that seems to be happening.

The analyst consensus calls for ASML's revenue to jump 56% to 11.7 billion euros, or $13.1 billion, and for adjusted earnings per share to nearly double from 5.49 euros to 10.76 euros. ASML's quarterly results are lumpy as its machines are very expensive and it sells around 100 of them each quarter. However, it also earns significant revenue from installed base management, which covers maintenance, repair, and upgrades to existing machines.

The forecast calls for ASML's strongest revenue growth since 2023, and significantly higher than the 24% growth it reported in the second quarter. The boom in memory explains part of the growth surge as the company has projected more than 75% growth in memory systems for the year, due to ramping demand for high bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, and top customers like TSMC and Intel are expanding production of more advanced nodes.

Is ASML a buy heading into earnings?

With the stock having roughly doubled over the last year, ASML can't be considered cheap anymore. It currently trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of 57, which is higher than many of its chip-stock peers, such as Nvidia, as well as ETFs that track the industry, such as the Van Eck Semiconductor ETF.

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) has had a great year so far. The average annual return of the S&P 500 is about 10%, and with it sitting at about 14.5% right now, it has been a good year. There are still a few months left, so the chances of it ending up even higher are quite good.

While the S&P 500 as a whole is doing well, a few individual performers stand out. Sandisk holds the title for best-performing S&P 500 stock this year, rising about 590% in 2026. Intel is another top performer, increasing nearly 200% so far this year. There are a handful of companies that also have had strong runs, including AMD.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

So, which stock will lead the S&P 500 higher next year? I think it will be a familiar face, and it won't be one of these three.

Image source: Getty Images.
Some stocks have gotten ahead of themselves

With the returns some stocks are delivering this year, it's pretty easy to guess that next year may not be as kind to these stocks. Many companies have far outgrown their business results and are trading at inflated valuations, such as Intel and AMD. These two trade for 70 and 81 times forward earnings, respectively. This showcases just how expensive they are. Others, like Sandisk, operate in a cyclical market, and the stock market is wary of giving it a standard valuation due to fears of the memory chip industry seeing a cyclical downturn.

Regardless, there are a handful of stocks that were abandoned to pave the way for these to rise, and the most obvious one is Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA). Nvidia led the S&P 500 in performance during 2023 and 2024, and I think it has a strong shot at leading it again in 2027. Why? Its stock has been ignored compared to some of its peers.

Nvidia is dirt cheap compared to its peers

It's hard to say that the largest company in the world by market cap isn't getting a fair shake, but that's exactly what's happening. As mentioned above, AMD trades at over 80 times forward earnings. Nvidia trades at 25.

AMD PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

These two companies operate in the same industry (namely, graphics processing units, or GPUs), and Nvidia is growing its data center business (the segment most exposed to artificial intelligence (AI)) at a faster pace. In Q2, Nvidia's data center division grew at a 117% pace to $89 billion. AMD's data center division grew at a 107% pace to $6.7 billion. Nvidia is still winning, and there's no reason to give AMD a ridiculous premium as a result.

title: What Does NVIDIA Offer That Marvell Does Not?
detail:
What Does NVIDIA Offer That Marvell Does Not?
Trefis Team

NVDA
AVGO
AMD
INTC
Explore stocks on Coinbase

Image from Pixabay

Investors buy Marvell Technology (MRVL) and NVIDIA (NVDA) to capture spending on artificial intelligence data centers, but the two companies generate revenue differently. NVIDIA sells the full AI system, while Marvell supplies custom chips for individual cloud customers and the components that connect chips inside a data center. Marvell has been the much stronger stock. It returned 222% over the past twelve months, compared with 25% for NVIDIA. What has each company told investors to expect from here?

What Marvell And NVIDIA Have Said Since August

Marvell recently raised its financial outlook, although NVIDIA still anticipates a faster pace of growth. On August 27, Marvell increased its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to roughly $12 billion and lifted its fiscal 2028 outlook to about $18 billion, up from $16.5 billion a quarter earlier. This new outlook means revenue growth of about 50% in fiscal 2028, and it includes the custom business more than doubling.

Then, on October 6, Marvell raised its fiscal 2028 outlook again, to about $20 billion, and forecast fiscal 2031 revenue of $70 billion to $90 billion during its Investor Day. For context, the company generated $9.5 billion in revenue over the past twelve months.

NVIDIA delivered a different kind of update on August 26. Management provided a forecast a year ahead for the first time, projecting revenue growth of about 70% in fiscal 2028, though they noted supply constraints would hold that figure back. NVIDIA had no earlier forecast to raise. During the same call, the company said rising memory costs would pull its gross margin from 75% to a low of 71% to 72% in the fourth quarter.

What Do Marvell And NVIDIA Give Up For Sales?

Both companies expect lower gross margins in the coming quarters. Marvell guided its fiscal Q3 2027 gross margin to between 57.5% and 58.5%, down from the 58.9% it reported for Q2, both on a non-GAAP basis. Management said the main reason is the custom business, which is ramping up quickly.

Even so, Marvell expects its profit to grow faster than its sales. On the August call, the finance chief said non-GAAP operating margin was likely to enter Marvell's 38% to 40% long-term target range in fiscal Q4 2027.

NVIDIA posted a gross margin of 75% in fiscal Q2 2027, and management expects it to bottom at 71% to 72% in Q4. The chip maker is also using its own balance sheet to back its customers. It has invested nearly $50 billion in frontier AI labs. Management expects AI labs to make up roughly a quarter of its business in the year ahead.

title: What Was Micron Telling You Before Its Stock Ran?
detail:
What Was Micron Telling You Before Its Stock Ran?
Trefis Team
Mon, October 12, 2026 at 9:33 AM PDT 3 min read
MU
WDC
INTC
NVDA
AMD
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Micron Technology (MU) stock returned 424.1% in the twelve months to October 9, 2026. That performance ultimately rested on a shortage of memory chips. Executives note that supply is tight and prices have been heading higher, with servers running artificial intelligence workloads serving as a big source of demand. How early could you have seen that demand coming?

Micron Was Talking About Servers Ten Months Early

The earliest sign emerged on December 18, 2024, during Micron's call for its fiscal first quarter of 2025. Executives described the company as a pioneering supplier of LP memory to the data center. The stock's run began almost ten months later on October 8, 2025.

Acting on that signal required nerve. During that same call, executives warned of near-term problems from market conditions and seasonality. By mid-April 2025, a Seeking Alpha article described a 35% decline in the stock since mid-January.

Yet evidence of the coming shift continued to mount. On April 17, 2025, Reuters reported that Micron was reshuffling its business units around AI-linked demand for memory chips from large-scale cloud providers. Then, on the June 25, 2025 call, executives noted that Micron had become the number two brand by share in data center SSDs.

Micron's Profit Margins Were Already Rising By October

The company's financial results confirmed this trajectory by early October 2025. During the September 23, 2025 call, executives stated that fiscal 2025 revenue grew nearly 50% to a record $37.4 billion. They also noted that gross margin had expanded by 17 percentage points to 41%.

The quarterly report filed on October 3, 2025, five days before the run began, showed the same improvement in profit. Operating margin reached 32.3% in the fiscal fourth quarter of 2025, up from 19.6% a year earlier.

Sales growth followed a less uniform path. Revenue rose 84.3% from a year earlier in the fiscal first quarter of 2025, but that growth slowed to 36.6% by the third quarter. It then picked up to 46.0% in the fourth.

Micron Took In $54.2 Billion In Three Months

Revenue in the latest quarter reached $54.2 billion, up 379.3% from a year earlier. Over the past twelve months, operating margin was 75%, compared with 26% in the twelve months before. While early statements indicated where demand was coming from, they did not reveal how large it would ultimately get.

The S&P 500 returned 17.0% over the same twelve months, yet Micron was not alone in outpacing the index. Among its peers, Western Digital returned 228.5% and Intel 179.7%. This industry-wide performance suggests investors were repricing more than Micron alone, making the company's own statements only one part of the broader market picture.
